1	/**
2	 * Inject `-e TYPE=<VARIANT>` into a Minecraft OsTemplate's setupScript from
3	 * `Server.gameVariant` (the customer's checkout choice — vanilla/paper/purpur/
4	 * fabric/forge, see lib/game-config.ts's MINECRAFT.variants).
5	 *
6	 * Found live 2026-08-30: this substitution never existed anywhere in the
7	 * provisioning pipeline. The OsTemplate's setupScript is one static string
8	 * with no `TYPE` at all, so `gameVariant` was captured at checkout, stored on
9	 * `Server`, and then completely ignored — every Minecraft customer got plain
10	 * Vanilla regardless of what they picked (or paid for a plugin-support tier
11	 * and had their manually-installed plugins never load, since Vanilla has no
12	 * plugin API at all). Diagnosed via a real customer ticket: the fix here is
13	 * minecraft-specific by design (it's the only family with a real variant
14	 * concept today) — generalize via `schemaFor(family)` if another family gains
15	 * one, rather than hardcoding a second family name here.
16	 *
17	 * Explicit and idempotent: always injects a `TYPE`, even for "vanilla" —
18	 * removes any reliance on the image's own default ever staying Vanilla — and
19	 * is a no-op if the script already names an explicit `TYPE` (never override
20	 * something a future per-family script sets on purpose).
21	 *
22	 * Kept in its own side-effect-free module (rather than inline in
23	 * worker/index.ts) so it can be unit tested directly — importing
24	 * worker/index.ts runs its top-level `main()` job-polling loop.
25	 */
26	import { randomBytes } from "node:crypto";
27	import { schemaFor, minecraftImageForVersion } from "../lib/game-config";
28	import { isGameFamily, controlSpec, isSafeRemotePath } from "../lib/game-control";
29	import { dayzSteamCredentials } from "../lib/dayz-steam";
30	import { applyPinToSetupScript, type PinPlan } from "../lib/mcjars/pin";
31	
32	function generatePassword(): string {
33	  // URL-safe, no ambiguous chars, 16 chars — same shape as worker/index.ts's
34	  // own generatePassword (kept as a small local copy rather than a shared
35	  // util, matching this codebase's existing convention — see also
36	  // worker/nxcloud.ts and lib/actions-company-mail.ts).
37	  return randomBytes(24).toString("base64url").replace(/[-_]/g, "x").slice(0, 16);
38	}
39	
40	export function applyGameVariant(setupScript: string, family: string | null, variant: string | null): string {
41	  if (family !== "minecraft") return setupScript;
42	  if (!variant) return setupScript;
43	  if (/-e\s+TYPE=/.test(setupScript)) return setupScript;
44	  const type = variant.toUpperCase();
45	  return setupScript.replace(/(docker run\s+(?:-d|--detach)\b)/, `$1 -e TYPE=${type}`);
46	}
47	
48	/**
49	 * Substitute the Minecraft image's Java-runtime tag to match the customer's
50	 * checkout-time VERSION choice.
51	 *
52	 * FOUND LIVE 2026-09-20: unlike every other customizable field, the
53	 * `itzg/minecraft-server` IMAGE TAG in `prisma/catalog.ts`'s setupScript is
54	 * not a `-e KEY=...` docker env var — it's the image reference itself — so
55	 * `applyGameConfigEnv` below (which only ever rewrites `-e KEY=` placeholders)
56	 * never touched it. Every Minecraft server was provisioned on the catalog's
57	 * static `:java21` regardless of the VERSION actually picked at checkout,
58	 * silently crash-looping any version needing a different Java (26.1+ needs
59	 * Java 25 — see lib/game-config.ts's MINECRAFT_JAVA_CUTOVERS for the real,
60	 * researched mapping and the live incident that found this).
61	 *
62	 * Deliberately minecraft-only and deliberately narrow: touches ONLY the
63	 * `itzg/minecraft-server(:tag)?` image reference, nothing else in the script.
64	 * Falls back to the schema's own VERSION default when the customer's
65	 * `gameConfig` doesn't carry one (an order that never touched the field) —
66	 * matching today's catalog default (1.21.1 -> java21) exactly, so a customer
67	 * who never touches VERSION sees no change in behavior.
68	 */
69	export function applyMinecraftJavaImage(
70	  setupScript: string,
71	  family: string | null,
72	  gameConfig: Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined
73	): string {
74	  if (family !== "minecraft") return setupScript;
75	  if (!/itzg\/minecraft-server(:[\w.-]+)?/.test(setupScript)) return setupScript;
76	  const version = gameConfig && gameConfig["VERSION"] != null ? String(gameConfig["VERSION"]) : "1.21.1";
77	  const image = minecraftImageForVersion(version);
78	  return setupScript.replace(/itzg\/minecraft-server(:[\w.-]+)?/, image);
79	}
80	
81	/**
82	 * The generalization this file's own docstring called for: substitute a
83	 * customer's checkout-time `Server.gameConfig` values into an OsTemplate's
84	 * setupScript, for whichever fields already appear in it as a docker
85	 * `-e KEY=...` env-var placeholder.
86	 *
87	 * Found live 2026-08-31 auditing DST (`dst` family): the whole per-family
88	 * customization schema in lib/game-config.ts (`ConfigField`, one per
89	 * `docker run -e KEY=...` in prisma/seed-wave4-games.ts and its Wave 1-3
90	 * predecessors) is captured at checkout into `Server.gameConfig`
91	 * (lib/game-order.ts) and shown in the post-deploy Settings tab, but — same
92	 * root cause as `applyGameVariant` above, just never generalized —
93	 * `provision()` in worker/index.ts never read it. Every family's setup
94	 * script always ran with its hardcoded static default (usually `''`),
95	 * regardless of what the customer entered at checkout. For most fields that
96	 * meant a cosmetically-wrong default (wrong MOTD, wrong hostname string);
97	 * for DST's `TOKEN` (an online DST cluster refuses to start with none — see
98	 * lib/game-config.ts's DST schema comment) it meant the container never
99	 * bound its port at all and PROVISION's own `checkGamePortOpen` health check
100	 * would time out and hard-fail the customer's paid order.
101	 *
102	 * Deliberately conservative: ONLY touches a key if the setupScript already
103	 * declares it as `-e KEY=...` — fields with no such placeholder (e.g. DST's
104	 * `PASSWORD`, which the yeetzone image never wired to an env var at all) are
105	 * left untouched rather than guessing a docker flag that isn't there.
106	 * Values are re-quoted as a single-quoted shell literal with proper `'`
107	 * escaping (`'\''`) so a customer-supplied string can never break out of the
108	 * quote and inject shell — the same safety property `validateConfig`'s own
109	 * control-character guard exists for, just extended to this second consumer
110	 * (a `docker run` command line) since the injection surface differs from a
111	 * line-oriented remote config file.
112	 */
113	/**
114	 * Substitute a freshly generated per-server secret into an OsTemplate's
115	 * setupScript, for a family whose image needs a real secret value that the
116	 * static catalog row can only ever leave blank — baking one directly into
117	 * the shared seed string (prisma/catalog.ts) would hand every future
118	 * customer the exact SAME value, since that row is one string shared by
119	 * every server of that family.
120	 *
121	 * Found live 2026-09-05 fixing a customer's "player list never loads"
122	 * ticket: the platform's own player-list/RCON feature (lib/game-control.ts)
123	 * requires Palworld's ADMIN_PASSWORD to be set (it doubles as the RCON auth
124	 * secret) and RCON's port published, but the catalog's setupScript set
125	 * neither — so no Palworld server, ever provisioned, could support the
126	 * player-list feature customers are paying for. RCON_ENABLED/RCON_PORT are
127	 * not secrets, so those went directly into prisma/catalog.ts's setupScript
128	 * string; only this one per-server value needs runtime substitution.
129	 *
130	 * Same conservative shape as applyGameConfigEnv: only touches a key that's
131	 * already present as `-e KEY=...` in the script, and the caller decides what
132	 * counts as a "secret" for a given family — this function has no per-family
133	 * knowledge of its own.
134	 */
135	export function applyGameControlSecrets(
136	  setupScript: string,
137	  secrets: Record<string, string>,
138	): string {
139	  let out = setupScript;
140	  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(secrets)) {
141	    const re = new RegExp(`-e\\s+${key}=(?:'[^']*'|"[^"]*"|\\S*)`);
142	    if (!re.test(out)) continue;
143	    const escaped = value.replace(/'/g, `'\\''`);
144	    out = out.replace(re, `-e ${key}='${escaped}'`);
145	  }
146	  return out;
147	}
148	
149	export function applyGameConfigEnv(
150	  setupScript: string,
151	  family: string | null,
152	  gameConfig: Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined,
153	): string {
154	  if (!family || !gameConfig) return setupScript;
155	  const schema = schemaFor(family);
156	  if (!schema) return setupScript;
157	  let out = setupScript;
158	  for (const field of schema.fields) {
159	    const raw = gameConfig[field.key];
160	    if (raw === undefined || raw === null) continue;
161	    // envKey lets a readable schema key (e.g. "world") differ from the
162	    // literal docker env var name the image expects (e.g. "WORLD_NAME") —
163	    // see ConfigField.envKey's doc comment in lib/game-config.ts.
164	    const envName = field.envKey ?? field.key;
165	    const re = new RegExp(`-e\\s+${envName}=(?:'[^']*'|"[^"]*"|\\S*)`);
166	    if (!re.test(out)) continue; // this field isn't docker-env-driven in this script — leave it alone
167	    const escaped = String(raw).replace(/'/g, `'\\''`);
168	    out = out.replace(re, `-e ${envName}='${escaped}'`);
169	  }
170	  return out;
171	}
172	
173	/**
174	 * If a GAME OsTemplate's setupScript installs the game via a detached
175	 * `docker run -d --name <container> ...` (true for every game image today —
176	 * see the OsTemplate rows for minecraft/terraria/ark/etc., all `docker run -d`),
177	 * rewrite the invocation to `docker create` and append a generated systemd unit
178	 * that starts/stops the container. Also caps the container's log driver
179	 * (`--log-opt max-size=10m --log-opt max-file=3`) — see the comment at the
180	 * `createCmd` line below for why.
181	 *
182	 * WHY THIS EXISTS: the whole game control panel — GAME_POWER start/stop/restart,
183	 * GAME_BACKUP, log tailing (lib/game-control.ts + worker/game-control.ts) —
184	 * resolves the running game exclusively via `systemctl cat <serviceHint>` /
185	 * `journalctl -u <unit>`. A bare `docker run -d` creates no systemd unit at all,
186	 * so every one of those lookups comes back empty and every control action fails
187	 * silently, on every game family, on every order. Found 2026-08-26 diagnosing a
188	 * customer's Terraria server (cmt9ss7ln000xhlrx0gch9fcx) that could never be
189	 * started/stopped from the dashboard even though PROVISION had completed
190	 * successfully — the container was in fact running, just entirely invisible to
191	 * systemd.
192	 *
193	 * The generated unit is named after the family's FIRST serviceHint, not the
194	 * docker container's own `--name` — the two don't always match (minecraft's
195	 * image runs as container "mc" but its control-spec hints are "minecraft" /
196	 * "minecraft-server") — so `systemctl cat <hint>` resolves regardless of what an
197	 * individual image's setup script happened to call its container.
198	 *
199	 * Intentionally conservative: any setupScript that doesn't match the exact
200	 * `docker run -d --name X ...` shape (or any non-game family, e.g. the
201	 * LAMP/WordPress/Caddy panel images that already install a real native systemd
202	 * service) is returned completely unchanged.
203	 *
204	 * Moved here from worker/index.ts 2026-09-24 (alongside `buildGameSetupScript`
205	 * below) so worker/game-control.ts — which worker/index.ts itself imports, so
206	 * it cannot import anything back from worker/index.ts without a circular
207	 * dependency — can also build a real reinstall script for the Danger Zone's
208	 * wipe/reinstall action. Purely a relocation: behavior is unchanged.
209	 */
210	export function wrapDockerGameService(setupScript: string, family: string | null): string {
211	  if (!isGameFamily(family)) return setupScript;
212	  const unitName = controlSpec(family)?.serviceHints[0];
213	  if (!unitName) return setupScript;
214	
215	  const re = /docker run\s+(?:-d|--detach)\b(.*?)\s+--name[= ]("?)([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\2(.*)$/.exec(setupScript.trim());
216	  if (!re) return setupScript;
217	  const [full, before, , containerName, after] = re;
218	  const matchIndex = setupScript.indexOf(full);
219	  if (matchIndex < 0) return setupScript;
220	
221	  // Strip docker's own restart policy — systemd now owns restart semantics for
222	  // this container, and leaving both in place makes the two supervisors fight
223	  // over a crash-looping process.
224	  const cleanedAfter = after.replace(/\s*--restart(?:=|\s+)\S+/, "");
225	  // Cap the container's json-file log driver. No game image's setupScript ever
226	  // set this, so a crash-looping container (systemd restarting it every 5s
227	  // forever — see RestartSec above) grows an unbounded log file. Root-caused
228	  // live 2026-09-17 on projectzomboid-kc0kcr: its docker json log alone had
229	  // grown to ~28 GB (on top of ~28.5 GB of rsyslog spamming its own
230	  // "no space left on device" write failures once the disk filled), filling
231	  // the 77 GB root disk to 100% and taking the game server down. This is the
232	  // single construction point every game family's `docker run` is rewritten
233	  // through, so applying the cap here covers all of them at once rather than
234	  // editing each family's setupScript individually. 10m x 3 files = a 30 MB
235	  // ceiling per container regardless of how long or how hard it crash-loops.
236	  const createCmd = `docker create --name ${containerName} --log-opt max-size=10m --log-opt max-file=3${before}${cleanedAfter}`
237	    .replace(/\s+/g, " ")
238	    .trim();
239	
240	  const prefix = setupScript.slice(0, matchIndex);
241	  const unit = [
242	    `cat > /etc/systemd/system/${unitName}.service <<'NXUNIT'`,
243	    "[Unit]",
244	    `Description=Nxeon game service (docker: ${containerName})`,
245	    "After=docker.service",
246	    "Requires=docker.service",
247	    "",
248	    "[Service]",
249	    `ExecStart=/usr/bin/docker start -a ${containerName}`,
250	    `ExecStop=/usr/bin/docker stop -t 30 ${containerName}`,
251	    "Restart=always",
252	    "RestartSec=5",
253	    "TimeoutStartSec=0",
254	    "",
255	    "[Install]",
256	    "WantedBy=multi-user.target",
257	    "NXUNIT",
258	    "systemctl daemon-reload",
259	    `systemctl enable --now ${unitName}`,
260	  ].join("\n");
261	
262	  return `${prefix}${createCmd}\n${unit}`;
263	}
264	
265	/**
266	 * Skip the Docker CE install when Docker is already on the guest.
267	 *
268	 * Every game setupScript starts `curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh && …`.
269	 * On a stock image that is the install (measured 2026-10-01 on node-5: ~25s
270	 * including the image pull). On a GOLDEN template (scripts/golden/) Docker is
271	 * baked in, and on a GAME_REINSTALL the guest already has it — re-running
272	 * get.docker.com there costs an apt update + a package reinstall (and may
273	 * restart dockerd) for nothing. Same exit-status semantics: the group
274	 * succeeds if Docker exists or the install succeeded.
275	 */
276	export function skipDockerInstallIfPresent(setupScript: string): string {
277	  return setupScript.replace(
278	    /curl -fsSL https:\/\/get\.docker\.com \| sh(?=\s*&&)/,
279	    "{ command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh; }"
280	  );
281	}
282	
283	/**
284	 * Minecraft JVM heap vs the VM's RAM.
285	 *
286	 * FOUND 2026-10-01: the catalog hardcodes `-e MEMORY=2G`, and itzg sets BOTH
287	 * -Xms and -Xmx from it, so on the 2 GB plan the JVM tries to commit the
288	 * entire VM's RAM as heap before the OS, dockerd and the JVM's own non-heap
289	 * memory get anything. Reproduced on a clean 2 GB VM with no swap: "There is
290	 * insufficient memory for the Java Runtime Environment to continue … failed to
291	 * map 2147483648 bytes", crash loop, NRestarts=78 in 10 minutes. A real order
292	 * only starts because every VM gets a RAM-sized swapfile — i.e. part of the
293	 * heap lives in swap. The opposite on the 8 GB plan: still a 2G heap, so the
294	 * customer paid for 8 GB and Minecraft could use 2.
295	 *
296	 * Rule: leave max(768 MB, 25%) of the VM for the OS + dockerd + JVM non-heap,
297	 * round down to 256 MB, never below 512 MB. A customer's explicit choice is
298	 * honoured but clamped to that ceiling; no choice (or the schema default "2G")
299	 * means "size it to my plan".
300	 */
301	export function minecraftMaxHeapMB(ramMB: number): number {
302	  const headroom = Math.max(768, Math.round(ramMB * 0.25));
303	  return Math.max(512, Math.floor((ramMB - headroom) / 256) * 256);
304	}
305	
306	/** Parse an itzg MEMORY value ("2G", "1536M", "1024m") into MB; null if unparseable. */
307	export function parseHeapMB(value: unknown): number | null {
308	  const m = /^\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*([GgMm])\s*$/.exec(String(value ?? ""));
309	  if (!m) return null;
310	  const n = Number(m[1]);
311	  return Math.round(m[2].toLowerCase() === "g" ? n * 1024 : n);
312	}
313	
314	export function applyMinecraftHeap(
315	  setupScript: string,
316	  family: string | null,
317	  gameConfig: Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined,
318	  ramMB: number | null | undefined,
319	): string {
320	  if (family !== "minecraft") return setupScript;
321	  if (!ramMB || !Number.isFinite(ramMB) || ramMB <= 0) return setupScript;
322	  const re = /-e\s+MEMORY=(?:'[^']*'|"[^"]*"|\S*)/;
323	  if (!re.test(setupScript)) return setupScript;
324	  const max = minecraftMaxHeapMB(ramMB);
325	  const chosenRaw = gameConfig ? gameConfig["MEMORY"] : undefined;
326	  const chosen = parseHeapMB(chosenRaw);
327	  const isDefault = chosenRaw === undefined || chosenRaw === null || String(chosenRaw) === "2G";
328	  const heap = isDefault || chosen === null ? max : Math.min(chosen, max);
329	  return setupScript.replace(re, `-e MEMORY='${heap}M'`);

332	/**
333	 * Catalog placeholder values for admin/RCON secrets that are the SAME on every
334	 * server of a family (prisma/seed-wave*.ts ship `changeme12`; images ship
335	 * `CHANGEME` / `docker`). Anyone who has read the seed files — or guessed —
336	 * knows them.
337	 */
338	export const WEAK_DEFAULT_SECRETS = new Set(["changeme12", "changeme", "CHANGEME", "docker", "admin", "password"]);
339	
340	/**
341	 * Admin-/RCON-grade env vars only — never join passwords (those are what the
342	 * customer hands their players, and are left exactly as configured).
343	 */
344	export function isAdminSecretEnvKey(envKey: string): boolean {
345	  if (!/(ADMIN|RCON)/.test(envKey)) return false;
346	  return /(PASS|PW)/.test(envKey);
347	}
348	
349	function scriptEnvValue(script: string, envKey: string): string | null {
350	  const m = new RegExp(`-e\\s+${envKey}=('[^']*'|"[^"]*"|\\S*)`).exec(script);
351	  if (!m) return null;
352	  return m[1].replace(/^['"]|['"]$/g, "");
353	}
354	
355	/**
356	 * Which schema fields of this family are admin/RCON secrets that the customer
357	 * left blank AND whose catalog placeholder is a weak shared default — i.e. the
358	 * server would otherwise boot with the same admin password as every other
359	 * server of that family. Returns schema FIELD keys; provision() mints a value
360	 * for each and persists it into Server.gameConfig, so it is (a) substituted by
361	 * applyGameConfigEnv like any customer value, (b) visible to the customer in
362	 * Settings, and (c) stable across PROVISION retries and GAME_REINSTALL.
363	 * Platform RCON is unaffected: it reads the password back out of the running
364	 * container's env (lib/game-control.ts `docker-env`).
365	 *
366	 * Found 2026-10-01: e.g. Project Zomboid ships `ADMIN_USERNAME=admin
367	 * ADMIN_PASSWORD=changeme12`, and ARK / ARK SA / Icarus / Soulmask / L4D2 /
368	 * TF2 ship the same `changeme12` as their admin/RCON password.
369	 */
370	export function adminSecretFieldsToMint(
371	  family: string | null,
372	  rawSetupScript: string | null,
373	  gameConfig: Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined,
374	): string[] {
375	  if (!family || !rawSetupScript) return [];
376	  const schema = schemaFor(family);
377	  if (!schema) return [];
378	  const out: string[] = [];
379	  for (const f of schema.fields) {
380	    if (f.type !== "string") continue;
381	    const envKey = f.envKey ?? f.key;
382	    if (!isAdminSecretEnvKey(envKey)) continue;
383	    const current = scriptEnvValue(rawSetupScript, envKey);
384	    if (current === null || !WEAK_DEFAULT_SECRETS.has(current)) continue;
385	    const chosen = gameConfig ? gameConfig[f.key] : undefined;
386	    if (chosen !== undefined && chosen !== null && String(chosen).trim() !== "" && !WEAK_DEFAULT_SECRETS.has(String(chosen))) continue;
387	    out.push(f.key);
388	  }
389	  return out;
390	}

392	/**
393	 * Backstop for admin/RCON env vars with NO schema field (nothing can be
394	 * persisted for the customer): if the final script still carries a weak
395	 * shared default, replace it with a fresh per-server value. Same
396	 * rotate-per-build rule as Palworld/Rust/CS2 below.
397	 */
398	export function rotateWeakAdminSecrets(setupScript: string): string {
399	  const re = /-e\s+([A-Z0-9_]+)=('[^']*'|"[^"]*"|\S*)/g;
400	  const secrets: Record<string, string> = {};
401	  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;
402	  while ((m = re.exec(setupScript))) {
403	    const value = m[2].replace(/^['"]|['"]$/g, "");
404	    if (isAdminSecretEnvKey(m[1]) && WEAK_DEFAULT_SECRETS.has(value)) secrets[m[1]] = generatePassword();
405	  }
406	  return Object.keys(secrets).length ? applyGameControlSecrets(setupScript, secrets) : setupScript;
407	}

409	/** One per-server secret, same generator as the family-specific ones below. */
410	export function mintGameSecret(): string {
411	  return generatePassword();
412	}

414	/**
415	 * Build the fully-substituted, systemd-wrapped game install script for a
416	 * server: variant → config values → Minecraft's java image tag → per-server
417	 * secrets → wrapped into a `docker create` + generated unit (see
418	 * `wrapDockerGameService`). Returns null for a non-game template (or one with
419	 * no setupScript at all).
420	 *
421	 * Extracted from `buildCloudInit` (2026-09-24) so `gameReinstall` (worker/
422	 * game-control.ts's GAME_REINSTALL handler) can regenerate the IDENTICAL
423	 * script an original PROVISION would have used — including reapplying
424	 * whatever gameVariant/gameConfig the customer has set SINCE the original
425	 * provision (a reinstall is exactly the moment a setting that silently never
426	 * applied gets a real chance to take effect), and minting BRAND NEW
427	 * per-server secrets for palworld/rust/cs2 on every call — the same
428	 * "reinstall rotates credentials, never keeps the old ones" rule
429	 * `reinstall()`'s own comment (worker/index.ts) applies to the VPS root
430	 * password.
431	 */
432	export function buildGameSetupScript(server: {
433	  osTemplate: { setupScript: string | null; family: string | null };
434	  gameVariant?: string | null;
435	  gameConfig?: unknown;
436	  /** Minecraft only: an exact mirrored jar to stage + pin (worker/mcjar-pin.ts#mcJarPinForSetup), or null for upstream behaviour. */
437	  __mcJarPin?: PinPlan | null;
438	  // The VM's real RAM (GamePlan.ramMB, else the VPS plan's). Optional: a
439	  // caller that doesn't load the plan (GAME_REINSTALL today) keeps the
440	  // catalog's heap exactly as before.
441	  // Index signature: callers pass their own partial selects (GAME_REINSTALL's
442	  // gamePlan is `{ gameFamily }`), which TS's weak-type check would reject.
443	  gamePlan?: { ramMB?: number | null; [k: string]: unknown } | null;
444	  plan?: { ramMB?: number | null; [k: string]: unknown } | null;
445	}): string | null {
446	  if (!server.osTemplate.setupScript) return null;
447	  const scriptWithDocker = skipDockerInstallIfPresent(server.osTemplate.setupScript);
448	  const scriptWithVariant = applyGameVariant(scriptWithDocker, server.osTemplate.family, server.gameVariant ?? null);
449	  const scriptWithConfig = applyGameConfigEnv(
450	    scriptWithVariant,
451	    server.osTemplate.family,
452	    server.gameConfig as Record<string, unknown> | null,
453	  );
454	  // Minecraft server-software mirror (lib/mcjars/pin.ts): stage the exact jar on
455	  // the guest and run it pinned, so container restarts never contact upstream
456	  // (2026-10-01 PaperMC outage). A pinned LATEST resolves to the concrete
457	  // version, and the Java image follows THAT version.
458	  const pin = server.osTemplate.family === "minecraft" ? server.__mcJarPin ?? null : null;
459	  const scriptWithPin = pin ? applyPinToSetupScript(scriptWithConfig, pin, server.gameVariant ?? "vanilla") : scriptWithConfig;
460	  const scriptWithJavaImageRaw = applyMinecraftJavaImage(
461	    scriptWithPin,
462	    server.osTemplate.family,
463	    pin
464	      ? { ...((server.gameConfig as Record<string, unknown> | null) ?? {}), VERSION: pin.mcVersion }
465	      : (server.gameConfig as Record<string, unknown> | null),
466	  );
467	  const scriptWithJavaImage = rotateWeakAdminSecrets(
468	    applyMinecraftHeap(
469	      scriptWithJavaImageRaw,
470	      server.osTemplate.family,
471	      server.gameConfig as Record<string, unknown> | null,
472	      (server.gamePlan?.ramMB as number | null | undefined) ?? (server.plan?.ramMB as number | null | undefined) ?? null,
473	    ),
474	  );
475	  // dayz (Wave 11, 2026-09-24): shared Nxeon-owned Steam credential, not a
476	  // freshly-generated per-server secret — see lib/dayz-steam.ts. Unconfigured
477	  // resolves to an empty object, so applyGameControlSecrets' "only touches a
478	  // key already present" discipline leaves the setupScript's blank
479	  // placeholders exactly as seeded (honest SteamCMD anonymous-login failure
480	  // rather than silently proceeding). lib/game-order.ts also refuses new DayZ
481	  // orders while unconfigured, so this branch should never actually run
482	  // against an unconfigured account in production.
483	  const dayzCreds = dayzSteamCredentials();
484	  const dayzSecrets: Record<string, string> = dayzCreds ? { USERNAME: dayzCreds.username, PASSWRD: dayzCreds.password } : {};
485	  const scriptWithSecrets =
486	    server.osTemplate.family === "palworld"
487	      ? applyGameControlSecrets(scriptWithJavaImage, { ADMIN_PASSWORD: generatePassword() })
488	      : server.osTemplate.family === "rust"
489	        ? applyGameControlSecrets(scriptWithJavaImage, { RUST_RCON_PASSWORD: generatePassword() })
490	        : server.osTemplate.family === "cs2"
491	          ? applyGameControlSecrets(scriptWithJavaImage, { CS2_RCONPW: generatePassword() })
492	          : server.osTemplate.family === "armareforger"
493	            ? applyGameControlSecrets(scriptWithJavaImage, { ADMIN_PASSWORD: generatePassword() })
494	            : server.osTemplate.family === "dayz"
495	              ? applyGameControlSecrets(scriptWithJavaImage, dayzSecrets)
496	              : scriptWithJavaImage;
497	  return wrapDockerGameService(scriptWithSecrets, server.osTemplate.family);
498	}
499	
500	/**
501	 * Extract the docker `--name X` container name from a family's RAW (pre-wrap)
502	 * `docker run -d --name X ...` setupScript — the exact same regex
503	 * `wrapDockerGameService` above uses, exposed separately for
504	 * `gameReinstall` (worker/game-control.ts), which needs the real container
505	 * name to `docker rm -f` the old one before recreating it. Returns null if the
506	 * script doesn't match that shape (defensive; every current game setupScript
507	 * does).
508	 */
509	export function dockerContainerNameFrom(setupScript: string): string | null {
510	  const re = /docker run\s+(?:-d|--detach)\b.*?\s+--name[= ]("?)([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\1/.exec(setupScript.trim());
511	  return re ? re[2] : null;
512	}
513	
514	/**
515	 * Extract every `-v hostpath:containerpath` HOST-side path from a family's
516	 * RAW setupScript — sourced straight from the real `docker run -v ...` flags
517	 * (never guessed), so these are exactly the directories the game's own
518	 * container persists data to and the only ones a genuine "wipe" needs to
519	 * clear. Host paths never contain a colon in any current family's script, so
520	 * matching up to the first `:` reliably isolates the host side even when the
521	 * container side is itself quoted-with-spaces (The Isle's setupScript does
522	 * this: `-v /opt/theisle:"/home/steam/.../The Isle Dedicated Server"`).
523	 *
524	 * Safety-guarded, not just parsed: only returns paths that are both
525	 * `isSafeRemotePath` AND at least two segments under `/opt/` (every real game
526	 * mount observed in prisma/seed-wave*.ts is `/opt/<family>[/subdir]`) — this
527	 * is deliberately narrower than `isSafeRemotePath` alone so a malformed or
528	 * hand-edited OsTemplate row can never make a "wipe" target something as
529	 * broad as `/`, `/opt`, `/home`, or `/root`.
530	 */
531	export function dockerHostMountsFrom(setupScript: string): string[] {
532	  const out: string[] = [];
533	  const re = /-v\s+([^\s:]+):/g;
534	  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;
535	  while ((m = re.exec(setupScript))) {
536	    const p = m[1];
537	    if (isSafeRemotePath(p) && /^\/opt\/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{2,}(\/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)*$/.test(p) && !out.includes(p)) {
538	      out.push(p);
539	    }
540	  }
541	  return out;
542	}

# FiveM managed hosting: legal/operational brief (observed 2026-10-01)

Not legal advice. Labels: CONFIRMED = primary source read directly; UNVERIFIED = only secondary/community sources, or not retrievable.
Local copy of the current agreement text: /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/pla.txt (pdftotext of the PDF).

## 0. Headline finding
fivem.net/terms currently 302-redirects to `https://static.cfx.re/platform-license-agreement-10-sept-2026.pdf` ("Last Updated: Sept. 10 2026", titled "Creator Platform License Agreement"). This is the current governing text (newer than the Jan 12 2026 version). The current text does NOT name Tebex or ZAP-Hosting; instead it reserves to Rockstar the right to designate "Authorized"/"exclusive" providers, "including ... server hosting", published on the Websites (s5.2). Older public statements (Oct 2024, Cfx staff) said ZAP-Hosting was the sole authorized game-server provider. The live page https://fivem.net/server-hosting now lists six "authorized hosting partners". So: a hosting company that is NOT on that list and sells FiveM servers is almost certainly in unauthorized territory.

## 1. Keymaster / server keys
- Free: "Generating server keys on keymaster.fivem.net is completely free." Source (secondary, hosting vendor doc): https://www.ouiheberg.com/en/documentation/article/keymaster-fivem-guide  -- UNVERIFIED against primary.
- Format: "a long string of alphanumeric characters (example: `cfxk_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx_xxxxxx`)" (same URL). UNVERIFIED primary.
- IP-bound: you must provide "the public IP address of your server" (no port); on IP change "you can update it in Keymaster, and 'the change is immediate.'" Same source; also https://www.doomhosting.com/help/articles/how-to-get-a-fivem-license-key and search summaries. UNVERIFIED primary.
- One key per server: "Each FiveM server must have its own unique key. Using a key on two servers simultaneously causes an authentication error." (ouiheberg). UNVERIFIED primary. Free accounts have limited key quotas.
- Needs a Cfx.re forum account; the portal is now portal.cfx.re (official docs: `sv_licenseKey` "Get one at portal.cfx.re").
- CONFIRMED (primary): https://docs.fivem.net/docs/server-manual/server-commands/ : "A string variable that sets the license key for this server. Get one at portal.cfx.re"
- CONFIRMED: PLA s6.3(1) uses the concept "Custom Servers for which you act as Server Admin and hold a corresponding server key".

## 2. PLA / hosting / reselling / responsible party
Source: https://static.cfx.re/platform-license-agreement-10-sept-2026.pdf (read via pdftotext).
- Hosting providers can be designated: s5.2 "Rockstar may identify certain third party service providers (including without limitation e-commerce, payment processor, server hosting, mod or asset marketplace, or gameplay video distribution platforms) as being either authorized or exclusive service providers for the Creator Service ('Authorized Service'). Rockstar reserves the right to require you to use an Authorized Service in connection with specific aspects of the Creator Service." and "Rockstar may identify certain third-party service providers as being unauthorized service providers ... Rockstar reserves the right to prohibit your use of any Unauthorized Service Provider". Changes "become effective thirty (30) days after being posted."
- Server owner = "Server Admin": s1.4 "A 'Server Admin' is a user who operates or assists in the operation or administration of a Custom Server." s4: "you are responsible for: (1) any Server Content ... (2) ensuring such Custom Server complies ... (3) ... all applicable laws". If Nxeon operates the server, Nxeon plausibly counts as a Server Admin ("operates or assists in the operation") and shares responsibility. (Interpretation.)
- License is personal/non-sublicensable: s2.1 "limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable, revocable license to access and use the Creator Services on compatible devices that you own or control." Hosting servers on Nxeon hardware for a customer sits awkwardly with "devices that you own or control". (Interpretation.)
- No branding: s2.3 "Without limiting the foregoing, you may not use such elements or intellectual property as part of the name or branding associated with a Custom Server. All websites, product listings, storefronts ... related to a Custom Server must: (1) clearly and conspicuously identify and provide a valid email contact for the individual(s) or entity that operates such Custom Server; and (2) include a clear and conspicuous disclaimer ... 'IS NOT APPROVED, SPONSORED, OR ENDORSED BY ROCKSTAR GAMES.'" and s2.2(2) bars use "as a brand, logo, or source identifier for goods or services in commerce".
- No explicit clause in the 10 Sept 2026 text banning resale of server hosting (searched for host/resell/resale). Earlier-version clause: Cfx staff (Yorick, forum, Oct 7 2024, https://forum.cfx.re/t/question-about-hosting-providers/5273092): "The only authorized provider for hosting FiveM **game** servers is ZAP-Hosting. This decision is final, and there is no option for negotiation with Cfx or Rockstar." and "Tebex is the exclusive monetization provider, while ZAP-Hosting is the sole Game Server Provider" (PLA s5.8 at the time). Community mod _4iY same thread: general hosting is fine "as long as FiveM (or Cfx) isn't mentioned or even alluded to _anywhere". (staff-quote CONFIRMED via forum fetch; the _4iY remark is a community member, not policy.)
- 2022 forum (https://forum.cfx.re/t/hosting-websites-reselling-fivem-hosting/4808936): termanator1128: "If they are selling game services then that is against TOS."; ChieF-TroN: "Selling FiveM/RedM game services is against ToS, specifically."
- Partner program: https://fivem.net/server-hosting says "Set up your server in under 5 minutes via one of our authorized hosting partners." Listed: GPORTAL, Shockbyte, Nitrado, Nodecraft, xREALM, ZAP-Hosting (extracted by fetch summariser; CONFIRMED-ish, re-check the page visually). No application process was found: UNVERIFIED how to become a partner.
- Also: a searched summary claims "You cannot sell any servers advertised as 'suitable for FiveM' or having FXServer preinstalled" (gameserverkings.com) -- UNVERIFIED, secondary.

## 3. Monetisation rules
Current text, s3.1 "Prohibited Methods" (same PDF): "(1) any mechanic that allows a user to pay or transfer ... Real Money to the Custom Server and subsequently receive ... Real Money ... ('Cash Out'), including Real Money gambling of any kind"; "(2) offering or selling for Real Money or in-game virtual currency any 'loot boxes,' 'gacha' elements, random drawings, or sweepstakes"; "(3) offering or selling in-game virtual currency for Real Money"; "(4) offering, selling, or facilitating access to Virtual Items (as defined in Section 4 of the Rockstar TOS) created by Rockstar"; "(5) operating a Custom Server by, on behalf of, or in an ongoing commercial association with, a third-party brand"; "(6) operating a website ... through which Server Content created by a third party ... is aggregated and sold or licensed to Server Admins for Real Money"; (7) third-party ads/sponsorships; (8) crypto/NFTs. "This list is not exhaustive; we reserve the right to modify or amend the list at any time".
- s3.2: commercial exploiters are "solely responsible for complying with all Rockstar policies as well as all laws ... consumer protection, ... collection of taxes, ... subscription services".
- Tebex: NOT named in the 10 Sept 2026 PDF (CONFIRMED by absence). Tebex-exclusive claim is from Oct 2024 staff post (above) citing old s5.8, and secondary sites (https://www.gameserverkings.com/knowledge-base/fivem/server-monetisation/). Treat as UNVERIFIED for current terms; s5.2 lets Rockstar mandate an Authorized Service anyway.
- Relevance to Nxeon: s3.1(6) and selling a managed server with pre-installed third-party scripts/mods could touch the "aggregated and sold" rule. Do not bundle paid third-party resources.

## 4. Rockstar / Take-Two
- The agreement is directly between the user and "Rockstar Games, Inc., its parent Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc." (PDF preamble). Rockstar acquired Cfx.re (announced Aug 2023; not re-verified here, widely reported -- UNVERIFIED primary).
- Changes: announcement Dec 22 2025, effective Jan 12 2026 ("We are updating our Platform License Agreement that governs your legal relationship with us and your use of Rockstar Games Creator Services."; "aligned with Rockstar Games' Terms of Service") https://forum.cfx.re/t/updates-to-the-creator-platform-license-agreement/5371920 ; Jan 12 2026 PDF https://static.cfx.re/platform-license-agreement-12-jan-2026.pdf ; further revision Sept 10 2026 (observed as current at fivem.net/terms redirect). I did not diff versions. Community commentary says the Jan 2026 text threatened virtual-item monetisation (https://www.prismnews.com/news/cfxre-creator-pla-update-threatens-fivem-and-redm-monetization-models), secondary.
- Creator Policies incorporate "the Rockstar Games Mod Guidelines" (s1.3). Not read.
- Rockstar mod marketplace for FiveM/RedM exists (https://respawn.outlookindia.com/gaming/gaming-news/rockstar-games-launches-official-mod-marketplace-fivem-redm) - secondary.

## 5. Element Club tiers
Primary: https://fivem.net/server-hosting (via fetch): "By default, servers support up to 48 players using OneSync Infinity"; Argentum $15/mo up to 64; Aurum $25/mo up to 128 w/ Infinity; Platinum $50/mo up to 2048 w/ Infinity. Docs: sv_maxclients "an integer from 1 to 2048" (server-commands page). Secondary (cfxre-tebex.io, search summary) says Argentum 64, Aurum 64/128, Platinum 128 (OneSync)/2048 (Infinity), and that Patreon billing ended Dec 1 2025 and moved to the Cfx Portal -- UNVERIFIED primary. Tiers are attached to the customer's Cfx account/key, not the host.

## 6. txAdmin
- Bundled with FXServer artifacts; port 40120 TCP; first start prints a 4-digit PIN; then link Cfx.re account (secondary: https://supercraft.host/wiki/fivem/txadmin_setup/ , https://nexus-games.com/us/blog/how-to-install-txadmin-fivem/). Official docs fetch only confirmed "Make sure a PIN is filled" (https://docs.fivem.net/docs/server-manual/setting-up-a-server-txadmin/). Port/PIN details: UNVERIFIED primary.
- Security guidance (secondary): firewall 40120 to admin IPs, or bind 127.0.0.1 and front with an authenticated reverse proxy. For Nxeon: never expose raw 40120 publicly; proxy via the panel.
- Artifact JSON also pins txAdmin versions (below).

## 7. Artifact JSON (live GET 2026-10-01, CONFIRMED)
`https://changelogs-live.fivem.net/api/changelog/versions/linux/server` returns:
`{"critical":"7290","recommended":"35245","optional":"7290","latest":"36897","critical_download":".../build_proot_linux/master/7290-a654bcc2.../fx.tar.xz","critical_txadmin":"7.0.0","recommended_download":".../master/35245-6efb47dff473c0e2a12fb50b08d74c0eb24a50d5/fx.tar.xz","recommended_txadmin":"8.1.1","optional_download":..., "optional_txadmin":"7.0.0","latest_download":".../master/36897-e34d12cd9a39cc223548a5be1ab09f60e9183051/fx.tar.xz","latest_txadmin":"8.1.1","support_policy":{"36897":"9999-12-31T23:59:59.9999999","36757":"2026-10-12T14:11:02Z", ...}}`
Fields: critical, recommended, optional, latest (build numbers); *_download (full URLs); *_txadmin (bundled txAdmin version); support_policy (build -> end-of-support timestamp; the latest never expires, older builds expire in days). URL scheme `https://runtime.fivem.net/artifacts/fivem/build_proot_linux/master/<build>-<40-hex-hash>/fx.tar.xz`. HEAD on latest: 200, application/x-xz, content-length 70,603,040 (~67 MiB), last-modified 2026-09-30. The directory index URL /master/ itself 301s to docs; no listing. Note "recommended" (35245) is far behind "latest" (36897); optional/critical are 7290 (ancient). Support policy implies the recommended build may fall out of support: UNVERIFIED how that is enforced, but plan to track `latest`/ recommended with a pin and test.

## 8. OneSync and HTTP endpoints
Docs (server-commands page): "`onesync [on/off/legacy]` -- Enables server-determined entity routing"; "Values at 32+ require OneSync enabled; values above 64 require OneSync set to 'on' mode" (summariser paraphrase) ; setup page: "set onesync on" "required for server-side state awareness". Whether OneSync is on by default in the txAdmin recipes: UNVERIFIED (recipes set it). Ports: `endpoint_add_tcp "0.0.0.0:30120"` / `endpoint_add_udp "0.0.0.0:30120"` (setup page, CONFIRMED).
Source code, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/citizenfx/fivem/master/code/components/citizen-server-impl/src/InfoHttpHandler.cpp (CONFIRMED, master today): `sv_requestParanoia` (0-3) gates /info.json, /dynamic.json, /players.json (level>=3 hides more); `sv_endpointPrivacy` "has been removed. Player endpoint addresses are no longer exposed on any HTTP endpoint."; `sv_exposePlayerIdentifiersInHttpEndpoint` "has been removed. Player names and identifiers are only exposed on `/players.json` when the request is authenticated via `sv_playersToken` (using the `X-Players-Token` header or `?token=` query parameter)." So public /players.json is now anonymised; use a token for panel player lists.

## 9. Hardware and competitor pricing (observed 2026-10-01)
- Official: "We recommend a x86-64 system running Linux or Windows (7/2008 R2+), decent upstream connectivity and preferably a multi-core processor." (https://fivem.net/server-hosting). No RAM figure in official docs found. Community norm 4-8 GB for 32-64 slots (UNVERIFIED).
- ZAP-Hosting (official partner): "FiveM server hosting from $8.93/Month"; lifetime from $78.53; txAdmin, FTP, DDoS included (https://www.zap-hosting.com/en/fivem-server-hosting/). Slot/RAM tiers not on page.
- GPORTAL (official partner): 10 slots $9.00/30d; 10 slots $24.30/90d; 48 slots $36.95/30d (Dallas) (https://www.g-portal.com/en/gameserver/fivem-server-hosting).
- Shockbyte (official partner): Sandy Shores 12 players 3GB $12.99/mo; Vespucci 24 players 4GB $15.99/mo; Vinewood unlimited 6GB $24.99/mo (https://shockbyte.com/games/fivem-server-hosting). License requirement not stated.
- RocketNode: from $6.50/mo 2 GB, 2 vCPU, 75 GB NVMe (search summary; live page showed no prices) (https://rocketnode.com/game-server-hosting/fivem) UNVERIFIED. NOT on the fivem.net partner list.
- GravelHost: $5/mo 3.5 GB; $7 6 GB; $23 12 GB (search summary, geekflare/others) UNVERIFIED. NOT on partner list.
- Nitrado: partner listed; pricing page URL 404/redirected, not obtained. VibeGAMES: not found (has a help article on buying a FiveM license; TLS error on fetch).
- Observation: unlisted hosts (RocketNode, GravelHost) openly sell FiveM, so enforcement practice differs from the written exclusivity; I found no evidence either way of enforcement actions. UNVERIFIED.

## 10. Go / no-go: "customer supplies own Keymaster key, Nxeon sells managed FiveM servers"
Assessment: NO-GO as a branded "FiveM hosting" product today; conditional/limited path only.
Reasons: (1) Rockstar can and historically did designate exclusive/authorized game-server hosting (s5.2; staff: "ZAP-Hosting is the sole Game Server Provider"; now six listed partners; Nxeon is not one), and may prohibit "Unauthorized Service Providers". (2) Customer-supplied key does not cure this: the key licenses the Server Admin, but Nxeon operating the server is selling the hosting service the policy reserves. (3) The licence is non-sublicensable and tied to devices the licensee "owns or controls" (s2.1). (4) Strict branding limits: no "FiveM"-style source identifier or Rockstar IP in product naming (s2.2-2.3), plus a disclaimer and operator contact required. (5) Terms change unilaterally, 30 days' notice, enforcement is "Adverse Action" against the customer's server/account (customers lose money, Nxeon gets support burden/reputational risk).
Lower-risk alternatives: (a) sell generic VPS/dedicated hosting with no FiveM marketing or preinstall (community claim: allowed if FiveM not mentioned; UNVERIFIED legally); customer installs FXServer and their own key. (b) Seek written permission/partner status from Rockstar/Cfx first (no public process found). (c) Get counsel review before any launch. Operationally it is easy (free artifacts, key per IP, txAdmin 40120 proxied), so the risk is purely contractual/enforcement, not technical.
If proceeding anyway: customer brings key and accepts the PLA; no preinstalled bundled paid scripts; never expose 40120 raw; set sv_requestParanoia/players token; update key IP after any migration; don't promise slots beyond the customer's Element Club tier.

/opt/nxeon-wt-fivem
# New marketing site (`/nxm`, staging only) — how pages are built and wired

The new site is the design package's own pages (`/root/nxeon-marketing-v1/src/New Marketing Website v1/nxeon-website-handoff`) ported by generators, with the owner's identity picks applied and **every price, plan, game, mod, post and region read from the system at request time**. Owner's rules: nothing hardcoded; SEO on every page (incl. dynamic ones); portal never touched; no production deploy until the whole site is ready; staging only (`app/nxm/layout.tsx` 404s outside `NXEON_ENV=staging`).

## Generators (never hand-edit their outputs)
- `python3 tools/nxm/port_home.py` → homepage (`app/nxm/page.tsx` + `_home/*`, `home.css`).
- `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py [slug ...]` → every inner page: runs the package's own builders, captures the page, then writes `app/nxm/_pages/<slug>/{page.css,content.ts,script.ts}` and the route file(s) `app/nxm/<route>/page.tsx`. Ends with a **real-data audit**: every page must say `wired` with no `stale` values before launch.
- Shared transforms: `tools/nxm/nxmlib.py` (routes, link mapping, CSS scoping, buttons, review/nav slots).

## Wiring a page to real data
1. **`tools/nxm/wire/<slug_with_underscores>.py`** — rewrites the design's snapshot data in the generated page:
   - `def body(html) -> html`: replace snapshot markup/values with slots `{{nxm:key}}` (escaped text) or `{{nxm:key:html}}` (trusted server-rendered markup).
   - `def js(src) -> src`: replace snapshot constants with values from `__NXM` (the page's data), e.g. `const(src, "VPS", "__NXM.vps")`. `__NXM` is parsed from `<script id="nxm-data">` before the page script runs.
   - `ALLOW = {...}`: `$`-amounts on the page that are NOT our prices (competitor prices with a source, a "$0.00 spent" illustration).
   - Use `_w.py` helpers (`sub`, `resub`, `const`): they assert the target exists, so a design change can never silently leave a snapshot value.
2. **`app/nxm/_data/<slug>.ts`** — the loader, server-only:
   - `export async function load(p: Record<string,string>): Promise<NxmLoad>` → `{ slots, data, jsonLd, crumb }`.
   - `export async function meta(p): Promise<Partial<SeoEntry> & {image?, type?}>` — REQUIRED for template routes (title/description from the item: mod name, post title…); optional for static pages whose SEO depends on live data.
   - Read data through the system's own modules (see below) — the same tables/helpers checkout and the live site use. Throw when required data is missing (fail closed); never fall back to a snapshot.
   - Deploy/buy links: `deployHref()` from `lib/deploy-intent.ts` with real ids (plan id, game family + tier id, region).
   - Shared helpers: `app/nxm/_data/lib.ts` (vpsPlans, vpsTermMap, gameTiers, gameName, liveRegions, usd, esc, introSpan, productLd, NxmLoad) and `cards.ts` (plan card renderers). Page-group helpers go in your own `_data/<group>-*.ts` file.
3. Re-run `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py <slug>` and check the audit line.

## Template routes (catalogues)
- A route with `[params]` in `ROUTES` (nxmlib) is served for every item; the loader gets `p` (e.g. `{family, slug}`) and must 404 unknown items (`notFound()` from `next/navigation`).
- A page fanned out to many fixed routes (e.g. one game template → `/rust-server-hosting`, …) is listed in `tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json`: `[{"route": "/rust-server-hosting", "params": {"family": "rust"}}]`.

## SEO (every page)
- `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts`: title/description/breadcrumb per production route (seeded from the live site's rendered metadata). Dynamic pages provide theirs via `meta()`.
- `nxmMetadata()` adds canonical (production route), OG/Twitter, noindex until launch.
- `NxmPage` emits BreadcrumbList (from the route), FAQPage (parsed from the page's own `<details><summary>` FAQ) and whatever `jsonLd` the loader returns (Product/AggregateOffer from real plans via `productLd`, BlogPosting, SoftwareApplication…). Match or exceed the live page's structured data (the live types per route are in docs/DOCUMENTATION.md → "New marketing site").

## Real data sources (use these, not copies)
- VPS: `db.plan` (active, sortOrder) + `lib/intro-pricing.ts` + `lib/billing-terms.ts` (`VPS_TERMS`, `termDiscountPct`) + `lib/annual-discount.ts`; disk add-on `lib/disk-expand.ts extraDiskPerGbCents()`; dedicated IPv4 `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`.
- Web hosting `db.hostingPlan`; email `db.emailPlan` (per-month = price/termMonths); NxCloud `db.nxCloudPlan`; the pricing explorer's combined view `lib/pricing-explorer-data.ts getPricingExplorerData()`.
- Domains: `POPULAR_TLDS` in `components/marketing/tlds.ts` ("from" prices; live search uses the registrar).
- Games: `lib/games.ts` (`GAME_FAMILIES`, `GAME_DISPLAY`, `GAME_ART_SLUG` → `public/games/art/*`, `GAME_GENRES`), tiers `db.gamePlan` (per family, per-month = price/termMonths), regions = enabled `db.node` rows + `lib/node-regions.ts` labels.
- Mods: `lib/mods-catalog.ts` (`queryCatalogMods`, `listCatalogFamilies`, `listFeaturedMods`, `listTopDownloadedMods`, `listRecentlyUpdatedMods`, `getCatalogMod`, `relatedCatalogMods`, …) — public = `active && upstreamOk`.
- Blog: `lib/blog.ts` (`getPublishedPosts`, `getPostsPage`, `getPublishedPost`, `renderArticle`, `getRelatedPosts`, `productLinkForPost`). Hide the internal `seobatch` tag from public tag lists.
- Contact: server action `submitContact` in `lib/actions-contact.ts` (categories `lib/contact-categories.ts`); newsletter `subscribe` in `lib/actions-newsletter.ts`.
- Status: `lib/monitoring.ts` + `lib/status-copy.ts`. Reviews: `app/nxm/_components/ReviewBadges.tsx` (real only).

## Verify
- Dev server on 3033 (shared): `curl http://localhost:3033/nxm<route>`; the port's audit; `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` (ignore `.next/types` noise); screenshots vs `dist/nxeon-<slug>.html` at 1440 and 390.

## Native pages (pages the design package doesn't include)

content.content:
# Environment Configuration

Starting from txAdmin v8.0.0, **you can now customize txAdmin through `TXHOST_*` environment variables** documented in this page.  
Those configurations are usually required for Game Server Providers (GSPs) and advanced server owners, and allow them to force txAdmin and FXServer to use specific ports/interfaces, customize the location of the txData directory, force a max player slot count, etc.  
  
> [!WARNING]
> The `txAdminPort`, `txAdminInterface`, and `txDataPath` ConVars, as well as the `txAdminZapConfig.json` file are now considered **deprecated** and will cease to work in an upcoming update.  
> If the new and old configs are present at the same time, the new one will take priority.  
> Setting `TXHOST_IGNORE_DEPRECATED_CONFIGS` to `true` will disable the old config and silence the respective warnings.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> All ConVars but `serverProfile` became `TXHOST_*` env vars, and you should avoid using it as the concept of txAdmin profiles will likely be deprecated soon.  
> If setting multiple servers, **we strongly encourage you to set up separate txDatas for your servers.** As otherwise the `admins.json` file will conflict.

> [!CAUTION]
> Although the configuration below is useful for Game Server Providers (GSPs), **this is in no way, shape, or form an endorsement or permission for anyone to become an unauthorized GSP**.  
> Please refer to the FiveM [Creator Platform License Agreement](https://fivem.net/terms).


## Setup

The specific way to set up those variables vary from system to system, and there are usually multiple ways even within the same system. But these should work for most people:  
- Windows:
    - Edit your existing `start_<version>_<profile>.bat` to add the `set VAR_NAME=VALUE` commands before the `./<...>/FXServer.exe` line.
    - Alternatively, you can create a `env.bat` file with the `set` commands, then start your server with `call env.bat && FXServer.exe`, which will run the `env.bat` before running `FXServer.exe`.
- Linux:
    - Edit your existing `run.sh` to add the  `export VAR_NAME=VALUE` commands before the `exec $SCRIPTPATH/[...]` line.
    - Alternatively, you can create a `env.sh` file with the `export` commands, then start your server with `source env.sh && ./run.sh`
- Docker: 
    - Create a `.env` file with the vars like: `VAR_NAME=VALUE`
    - Load it using the `--env-file=.env` flag in your docker run command.
- Pterodactyl: You will likely need to contact your GSP or edit the "egg" being used.

> [!TIP]
> For security reasons, those environment variables **should** be set specifically for the boot process and **must not** be widely available for other processes.
> If they are to be written to a file (such as `.env`), the file should only be readable for the txAdmin process and not its children processes. 


## Variables Available

### General
- **TXHOST_DATA_PATH**
    - **Default value:** 
        - **Windows:** `<fxserver_root>/../txData` — sits in the folder parent of the folder containing `fxserver.exe` (aka "the artifact").
        - **Linux:** `<fxserver_root>/../../../txData` — sits in the folder that contains your `run.sh`.
    - The path to the txData folder, which contains the txAdmin logs, configs, and data. This is also the default place suggested for deploying new servers (as a subfolder). It is usually set to `/home/container` when running on Pterodactyl.
    - <mark>NOTE:</mark> This variable takes priority over the deprecated `txDataPath` ConVar.
- **TXHOST_GAME_NAME**
    - **Default value:** _undefined_.
    - **Options:** `['fivem','redm']`.
    - Restricts to only running either FiveM or RedM servers.
    - The setup page will only show recipes for the game specified
- **TXHOST_MAX_SLOTS**
    - **Default value:** _undefined_.
    - Enforces the server `sv_maxClients` is set to a number less than or equal to the variable value.
- **TXHOST_QUIET_MODE**
    - **Default value:** `false`.
    - If true, do not pipe the FXServer's stdout/stderr to txAdmin's stdout, meaning that you will only be able to see the server output by visiting the txAdmin Live Console page.
    - If enabled, server owners won't be able to disable it in `txAdmin -> Settings -> FXServer` page.
    - <mark>NOTE:</mark> We recommend that Game Server Providers enable this option.
- **TXHOST_API_TOKEN**
    - **Default value:** _undefined_.
    - **Options:** `disabled` or a string matching `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,48}$/`.
    - The token to be able to access the `/host/status` endpoint via the `x-txadmin-envtoken` HTTP header, or the `?envtoken=` URL parameter.
    - If token is _undefined_: endpoint disabled & unavailable.
    - If token is string `disabled`: endpoint will be publicly available without any restrictions.
    - If token is present: endpoint requires the token to be present.

### Networking
- **TXHOST_TXA_URL:**
    - **Default value:** _undefined_.
    - If present, that is the URL that will show on txAdmin as its public URL on the boot message.
    - This is useful for when running inside a container using `0.0.0.0:40120` as interface/port.
- **TXHOST_TXA_PORT**
    - **Default value:** `40120`.
    - Which TCP port txAdmin should bind & listen to.
    - This variable cannot be `30120` to prevent user confusion.
    - <mark>NOTE:</mark> This variable takes priority over the deprecated `txAdminPort` ConVar.
- **TXHOST_FXS_PORT**
    - **Default value:** _undefined_.
    - Forces the FXServer to bind to the specified port by enforcing or replacing the `endpoint_add_*` commands in `server.cfg`.
    - This variable cannot be `40120` to prevent user confusion.
- **TXHOST_INTERFACE**
    - **Default value:** `0.0.0.0`.
    - Which interface txAdmin will bind and enforce FXServer to bind to.
    - <mark>NOTE:</mark> This variable takes priority over the deprecated `txAdminInterface` ConVar.

### Provider
- **TXHOST_PROVIDER_NAME**
    - **Default value:** `Host Config`.
    - A short name to identify this hosting provider.
    - The value must be between 2 and 16 characters long and can only contain letters, numbers, underscores, periods, hyphens, and spaces. Must not start or end with special chars, and must not have two subsequent special chars.
    - This will usually show in warnings regarding configuration or user actions that go against any `TXHOST_*` variable.
- **TXHOST_PROVIDER_LOGO**
    - **Default value:** _undefined_.
    - The URL for the hosting provider logo which will appear at the login page.
    - The maximum image size is **224x96**.
    - You can create a theme-aware URL by including a `{theme}` placeholder in the URL, which will be replaced by `light` or `dark` at runtime, depending on the theme being used, eg. `https://.../logo_{theme}.png`.


### Defaults 
- **TXHOST_DEFAULT_DB<HOST|PORT|USER|PASS|NAME>**
    - **Default value:** _undefined_.
    - To be used only for auto-filling the config steps when deploying a new server and can be overwritten during manual deployment or after that by modifying their `server.cfg`.
    - All the values will be considered strings, and no validation will be done to them.
- **TXHOST_DEFAULT_CFXKEY**
    - **Default value:** _undefined_.
    - To be used only for auto-filling the config steps when deploying a new server and can be overwritten during manual deployment or after that by modifying their `server.cfg`.
    - The value should be a `cfxk_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx_xxxxxx` key, which individuals can obtain in the [Cfx.re Portal](https://portal.cfx.re/).
    - This is also very useful for developers who need to go through the txAdmin Setup & Deployer frequently.
- **TXHOST_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT**
    - **Default value:** _undefined_.
    - This variable is used by GSPs for setting up an `admins.json` automatically on first boot.
    - It contains a username, FiveM ID, and password (as bcrypt hash) separated by colons:
        - **Username:** If a FiveM ID is provided, this must match the username of the FiveM account used by the second parameter. Otherwise, it accepts any username valid for txAdmin accounts (same rule used by the [FiveM Forum](https://forum.cfx.re/)).
        - **FiveM ID:** The numeric ID of a FiveM account, same as the one visible as in-game identifier. For instance, the value should be `271816` for someone with the in-game identifier `fivem:271816`. When set, the admin will be able to login using the Cfx.re button instead of requiring a password.
        - **Password:** A bcrypt-hashed password to be used as the "backup password".
    - The account must at least have either FiveM ID or password set. If an account has no password, on first access the owner will be queried to change their password.
    - Examples:
        - `tabarra:271816`
        - `tabarra:271816:$2a$11$K3HwDzkoUfhU6.W.tScfhOLEtR5uNc9qpQ685emtERx3dZ7fmgXCy`
        - `tabarra::$2a$11$K3HwDzkoUfhU6.W.tScfhOLEtR5uNc9qpQ685emtERx3dZ7fmgXCy`

> [!NOTE]  
> More variables are still being considered, like options to configure reverse proxy IPs, security locks, etc.  
> Please feel free to provide feedback and suggestions.


## Examples

### Migrate old `start.bat`
Replace this:
```batch
@echo off
"E:/FiveM/13079//FXServer.exe" +set serverProfile "server2" +set txAdminPort "40125"
pause
```
With this:
```batch
@echo off
set TXHOST_DATA_PATH=E:\FiveM\txData-dev
set TXHOST_TXA_PORT=40125
"E:/FiveM/13079//FXServer.exe"
pause
```
> [!NOTE]
> Replace `"E:/FiveM/13079//FXServer.exe"` with the path you see in your existing `*.bat`.

That's a great primary source, and the caution note explicitly disclaiming that it grants permission to become an unauthorized GSP is an important quote for the legal document. I'm also noting a key design detail: TXHOST_INTERFACE binds both txAdmin and FXServer to the same interface, so you can't bind txAdmin to localhost alone while FXServer listens on all interfaces using that variable in Docker.

With the container's internal interface open but only the game port published publicly and txAdmin's port published to loopback only, txAdmin becomes reachable solely via SSH tunnel from the VM, which is a documented access pattern (with a proxy as a possible future addition). I'm also weighing two run modes — a txAdmin-managed mode where it owns server.cfg generation through its setup wizard, versus a plain mode where our platform generates and owns server.cfg directly via FXServer's exec flag — and considering which should be the default.

I'm settling on plain mode as the default since it's deterministic and lets readiness probes work without manual intervention, while making txAdmin an optional toggle that boots FXServer without the exec flag so txAdmin's monitor starts and prints a PIN for the customer to use when selecting "Existing server data" pointed at our generated config. I'm also working out the relevant TXHOST_ environment variables for slots, keys, provider name, quiet mode, data path, and port, and now I need to check how txAdmin actually prints its PIN in the logs so I can parse it correctly.

#!/bin/bash
# Two-slot lock so at most TWO heavy jobs (tsc, next dev, playwright, test suites) run at once on this box.
# This machine is the live production primary (also hosts customer VMs) — uncontrolled parallel tsc/dev servers
# can OOM or starve production. (Was 1 slot; raised to 2 on 2026-10-01 because 20 agents were queueing.)
# usage: heavy.sh bash -c "cd /opt/nxeon-wt-foo && npx tsc --noEmit -p ."
deadline=$((SECONDS + 3600))
while [ $SECONDS -lt $deadline ]; do
  for i in 1 2; do
    exec {fd}>/tmp/nxeon-heavy.$i.lock
    if flock -n $fd; then
      exec nice -n 19 ionice -c3 env NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=3072" "$@"
    fi
    exec {fd}>&-
  done
  sleep 2
done
echo "heavy.sh: timed out waiting for a slot" >&2; exit 75

Now I'm mapping out FiveM licence tiers and their slot caps: default, argentum, aurum, and platinum, each with different limits depending on whether OneSync Legacy or OneSync Infinity is enabled — default tops out at 48 with Infinity, while platinum can reach 2048. I'm also noting that slot counts above 32 require OneSync to be enabled at all.

Pulling exact slot caps from the plan pages: Argentum tops out at 64 with OneSync Infinity, Aurum at 64/128, Platinum at 128/2048, and default tier at 48 with Infinity. Since legacy/off caps aren't clearly documented, I'll mark those as unverified and default them to 32, noting the uncertainty in comments.

Since the schema's max client field is static but the plan's actual slot cap is dynamic, I need a separate validation function that checks slot capacity against the plan, called both during quote creation and config saving. I'm designing a single server-only function that takes the submitted values, previous config, and plan slots, returning either the validated values or an error, to be invoked from both the game-order and save-config flows -- now I'm checking whether the checkout wizard actually requires the license key to be present before validation runs.

Instead, I'll render the full server.cfg in TypeScript at provisioning time and inject it as base64 into the setup script, which decodes it onto the guest. For future config updates, the TS renderer stays the single source of truth: it rewrites server.cfg over SSH and restarts. The container's startup script stays minimal, just executing the FiveM runtime with server.cfg, and even the txAdmin mode toggle gets read from a file rather than a docker env var so it can change without recreating the container. Writing nx-start.sh...

Now I'm sketching the nx-artifact.sh script, which sources channel/build config and handles install/update cases, printing NXFA: status markers as it progresses.

Fetching the changelog JSON from FiveM's API to get the latest build version for the server. For parsing it without jq, I'm relying on python3, which is guaranteed present since cloud-init requires it on all these cloud images.

Pinning to an arbitrary build is actually tricky since the changelog API only exposes current channel builds, not historical ones by hash. I'm checking whether there's a way to query a specific build number directly, but it seems impractical -- the artifact directory listings redirect to docs instead of showing raw files, so I should simplify "pinning" to just mean freezing whatever the current build is rather than supporting arbitrary version numbers.

I'll make artifactBuild an enum restricted to the known builds, relabeled as "Pin build," with options sourced from the known artifacts table. I should also flag that pinning to a build whose support window has expired could cause Cfx to reject connections as outdated, and need to handle validating the resolved URL and build info during the download step.

For the download itself, I'm writing logic to fetch the artifact securely with curl, verify its size and hash, validate the tarball contents to ensure it only contains expected paths like alpine/ and run.sh with no traversal or absolute paths, confirm FXServer binary is present, check against an optional pinned SHA256, then extract to a staging directory and atomically swap it into place as the new artifact.

But I realize the tricky part is that the live artifact directory is bind-mounted into the running container, so simply renaming directories on the host won't update what the container sees until it's restarted — and deleting the old directory while the server still has files open there could break things mid-run. So the safe update flow needs to download and verify into the new directory first, then restart the service so Docker re-resolves the bind mount to the new path, only cleaning up the old directory afterward.

Since I can't customize the generated systemd unit's ExecStartPre, I'll handle this inside my own update command instead: fetch into a staging directory, then stop the service, swap the directories, and let the common tail restart it — so downtime is limited to just the swap step. I'll also keep the previous artifact around for rollback rather than deleting it immediately, only purging older generations.

I realize there's a bug risk: if swap fails after the service was stopped for a staged artifact, the service needs to be explicitly restarted in that failure path so it doesn't stay down. For install/provision mode, it's simpler—just fetch and swap directly since nothing is running yet, and I should verify the default resource repo (cfx-server-data) and its license/URL.

def build(slug):
    cap = {}
    real_open, real_b64 = builtins.open, base64.b64encode
    class Cap(io.StringIO):
        def __init__(self, key): super().__init__(); self.key = key
        def close(self): cap[self.key] = self.getvalue(); super().close()
        def __exit__(self, *a): self.close()
    def fake_open(path, mode="r", *a, **k):
        p = str(path)
        if "w" in mode and ("/dist/" in p or os.path.basename(p).startswith("test")):
            return Cap(os.path.basename(p))
        return real_open(path, mode, *a, **k)
    cwd = os.getcwd(); os.chdir(SRC)
    builtins.open, base64.b64encode = fake_open, _fake_b64
    try:
        if slug == "game-servers":
            sys.argv = ["build_games2.py"]; runpy.run_path("build_games2.py", run_name="__main__")
        else:
            sys.argv = ["build_page.py", slug]; runpy.run_path("build_page.py", run_name="__main__")
    finally:
        builtins.open, base64.b64encode = real_open, real_b64
        os.chdir(cwd)
    html = next(v for k, v in cap.items() if k.startswith("nxeon-"))
    return html

# ── native pages: pages the design package doesn't include ─────────────────
# Authored in the package's own page format (body.html with {{SPRITE}}/{{NAV}}/
# {{FOOTER}}, page.css, page.js, meta.json) under tools/nxm/native/<slug>/ and
# assembled exactly like the package's build_page.py: shared shell + common.css
# + aurora + the page's own css/js. Then the same pipeline as every page.
NATIVE = f"{os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))}/native"
def build_native(slug):
    D = f"{NATIVE}/{slug}/"
    meta = json.load(open(D + "meta.json"))
    p1, p2, p3 = (open(f"{SRC}/part{i}.html").read() for i in (1, 2, 3))
    MAIN = "https://claude.ai/artifact/KryegJ1sG3zYzX7MyxypYs"
    head = re.sub(r"<title>.*?</title>", f"<title>{meta['title']}</title>", p1, count=1)
    head = re.sub(r'<meta name="description" content="[^"]*">', f'<meta name="description" content="{meta["description"]}">', head, count=1)
    head = head.replace('url("__IMG_HERO2__")', "none").replace('url("__IMG_GRAIN__")', "none")
    css = open(f"{SRC}/pages/common.css").read() + AURORA_CSS + (open(D + "page.css").read() if os.path.exists(D + "page.css") else "")
    print(f"{slug:36} {BASE}{route if route != '/' else ''}  css {len(css_out)//1024}KB  body {len(body)//1024}KB  "
          f"js {len(js)//1024}KB  buttons {btns}  reviews {nrev}")
    return slug

# ── routes ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A page is a TEMPLATE when its route has [params] (e.g. /mods/[family]/[slug])
# or when tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json fans it out to many fixed routes
# (e.g. the game template -> /rust-server-hosting {family: "rust"}, ...).
# Loaders get the params: load(p) / meta(p).
def routes_for(slug):
    f = f"{os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))}/routes/{slug}.json"
    if os.path.exists(f):
        return [(e["route"], e.get("params", {})) for e in json.load(open(f))]
    return [(ROUTES[slug], {})]

def write_route(slug, route, fixed, loader):
    """One route file. Every route passes its [params], fixed template params
    and ?query (search, pagination, ?topic= deep links…) into the loader as one
    map; the concrete path (/mods/[family]/[slug] -> /mods/minecraft/lithium)
    is used for canonical and breadcrumbs."""
    rd = f"{ROOT}/app/nxm{route}"; os.makedirs(rd, exist_ok=True)
    rel = os.path.relpath(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm", rd)
    pc = PARTICLES.get(slug)
    particles = f' particles={{{{ from: "{pc[0]}", to: "{pc[1]}" }}}}' if pc else ""
    # loader-supplied colours (e.g. per game) win over the slug default
    pdefault = f' ?? {{ from: "{pc[0]}", to: "{pc[1]}" }}' if pc else ""

# FiveM hosting: legal and operational brief

Date: 2026-10-01. Branch: `feature/fivem-game-server`. Status: built behind a flag that is off by default (`FIVEM_ENABLED`). Nothing is seeded and nothing is sold.

This is not legal advice. Labels used below:
- **CONFIRMED**: read directly in a primary source, which is quoted.
- **UNVERIFIED**: only secondary or community sources, or a claim that could not be retrieved.

## 1. Verdict

**NO-GO for launch until the owner has written permission from Cfx.re/Rockstar, or partner status with them.** If that cannot be had, counsel must sign off instead.

The terms do not contain a sentence saying "hosting companies may not resell FiveM servers". They do give Rockstar the power to name the only hosts allowed, and Cfx.re has publicly used that power. Nxeon is not on the list.

The rule "if the terms genuinely forbid reselling, stop before wiring checkout" was applied as follows:
- **Checkout is wired, but closed.** `lib/game-order.ts` refuses every fivem order unless `FIVEM_ENABLED=1`.
- **No plans exist.** No GamePlan/OsTemplate row exists anywhere. `prisma/seed-fivem.ts` refuses to run without both `FIVEM_ENABLED=1` and `FIVEM_SEED_CONFIRM=yes`.
- **No public page.** No marketing page is published, nothing is in the sitemap and nothing is in live-routes.

Why it is NO-GO:

Rockstar reserves the right to require you to use an Authorized Service in connection with specific aspects of the Creator Service. … Rockstar may identify certain third-party service providers as being unauthorized service providers ("Unauthorized Service Provider"). Rockstar reserves the right to prohibit your use of any Unauthorized Service Provider in connection with the Creator Service. … any such changes … will become effective thirty (30) days after being posted."

The partners shown are GPORTAL, Shockbyte, Nitrado, Nodecraft, xREALM and ZAP-Hosting. No application process was found (UNVERIFIED that none exists).
3. **Cfx.re's own software says this.** This is CONFIRMED in the txAdmin documentation shipped inside the official FXServer artifact (build 35245, `citizen/system_resources/monitor/docs/env-config.md`):
   > "Although the configuration below is useful for Game Server Providers (GSPs), **this is in no way, shape, or form an endorsement or permission for anyone to become an unauthorized GSP**. Please refer to the FiveM Creator Platform License Agreement."

A "Server Admin" is "a user who operates or assists in the operation or administration of a Custom Server" (s1.4). Section 4 makes the Server Admin responsible for the server. Nxeon running the server plausibly makes Nxeon a Server Admin too. That is our reading, not a quoted rule.

- **Best:** written permission or partner status from Cfx.re/Rockstar. The repo has no contact; the owner must start this. No email was sent.
